request: Make slugkit simple to use. People keep getting it wrong. It belongs under Feature #90 (Developer experience).

exchanges.say: You want slugkit to be simple. "Simple" for a library means the calls and options a first-time user needs before the first result. Today the only export is createSlugger(options) (export:slugkit), which throws unless all five options are given. Three questions, riskiest first.

questions.ask: What should a first-time user write to get a first slug? Today the one export is createSlugger(options) (export:slugkit), and it needs all five options.
questions.default: One import and one call with defaults, because the README's first example is what everyone copies.

questions.ask: How do people get it wrong today, and must createSlugger keep working as it does for existing users (test:test/index.test.js)?
Which options can have defaults, and what should each default be?
questions.default: A dash, lowercase, and no length limit, because that is what the README example passes today.

answers.text: One import and one call: `slugify('Hello World')` should give 'hello-world', and that should be the first example in the README.
Today they copy the README and forget one of the five options, then get `invalid options`. Keep createSlugger working exactly as it does for people who already use it.
Every option should be optional: a dash, lowercase, and no length limit unless you ask.

exchanges.say: So: one import and one call, `slugify('Hello World')` giving 'hello-world', with a dash, lowercase, and no length limit by default, and createSlugger unchanged. Two more.

questions.ask: Are any option names confusing, such as transliterate?
Is this only the first call and its defaults, with no new options?

answers.text: Only the first-use path and the defaults. No new options.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like. Goal: a first-time user gets a slug from one import and one call. Done when: `slugify('Hello World')` returns 'hello-world' with no options; its defaults are a dash, lowercase, and no length limit; the existing createSlugger tests pass unchanged; and the README's first example is those two lines. Checkpoints: the one-call slug, then the unchanged tests, then the README. Renaming options is parked.
